- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+10% from prior 10d mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7d horizon.
- If supply_net is strongly negative (e.g., < -20) and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates upside; add +3–5% to forecast mean for 30d horizon.
- When sentiment is mixed or bearish (≤0.33) and supply_net is negative, model tends to underestimate true price decline; apply +1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >+10% above recent 10d average, reduce forecast by 5–10% to align with historical volatility.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply_net, model often overestimates volatility; cap forecast at 10% above 30d moving average to avoid overextension.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag in direction; adjust forecast to match sentiment swing direction by 1–2 days lag.
